When $x=2$, $y=\left(2+\frac{2}{2}\right)^2=9$

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{373_q17_s2}

$P(1\text{ turn})=\dfrac{4}{7}$

$P(2\text{ turns or less})=\dfrac{4}{7}+\dfrac{3}{7}\times\dfrac{4}{7}\times\dfrac{4}{7}=\dfrac{4}{7}+\dfrac{3}{7}\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^2$

$P(3\text{ turns or less})=\dfrac{4}{7}+\dfrac{3}{7}\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)^2\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^3$

$P(4\text{ turns or less})=\dfrac{4}{7}+\dfrac{3}{7}\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)^2\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^3+\left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)^3\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^4$

$\therefore P(n\text{ turns or less})=\dfrac{4}{7}+\dfrac{3}{7}\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^2+\dots+\left(\dfrac{3}{7}\right)^{n-1}\left(\dfrac{4}{7}\right)^n$, a GP with $r=\dfrac{3}{7}\times\dfrac{4}{7}$

$P(\text{Ms Kim wins the game})=$ limiting sum of the GP

$S_\infty=\dfrac{\frac{4}{7}}{1-\frac{3}{7}\times\frac{4}{7}}=\dfrac{28}{37}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct answer; 2: correct limiting sum expression; 1: identifies a GP with r = (3/7)(4/7)
2: correct proof; 1: combines fractions and uses cos^2 = 1 - sin^2

In $\triangle ADC$: $\dfrac{AC}{\sin60^\circ}=\dfrac{y}{\sin45^\circ}$, so $\dfrac{AC}{\frac{\sqrt3}{2}}=\dfrac{y}{\frac{1}{\sqrt2}}$, $\dfrac{2AC}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt2y$

solutions.latex:
Area$_{\triangle ABC}=\dfrac12\times x\times AC\times\sin(105^\circ)$

Area$_{\triangle ADC}=\dfrac12\times AC\times y\times\sin(75^\circ)$

$\therefore\dfrac{A_{\triangle ABC}}{A_{\triangle ADC}}=\dfrac{\frac12xAC\sin(105^\circ)}{\frac12yAC\sin(75^\circ)}$

solutions.latex:
$y=\sin x\ \to\ y=\dfrac12-\dfrac12\cos(2x)$

\begin{itemize}
\item $\sin(x)\to\cos(x)$, since $\cos(x)=\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)$: this step requires a horizontal translation to the right by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
\item $\cos(x)\to\cos(2x)$: this step requires a horizontal compression by a factor of 2.
\item $\cos(2x)\to-\dfrac12\cos(2x)$: this step requires a vertical reflection and a vertical compression by a factor of 2.
\item $-\dfrac12\cos(2x)\to\dfrac12-\dfrac12\cos(2x)$: this step requires a vertical translation of $\dfrac12$ in the upwards direction.
\end{itemize}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: translation of sin x to cos x; 1: horizontal compression, reflection and vertical compression; 1: vertical translation up 1/2
review_reasons: Guide's first step is questionable: shifting sin x right by pi/2 gives -cos x, not cos x (cos x = sin(x + pi/2)); transcribed as written

solutions.latex:
Stat. points: let $f'(x)=0$

$f'(x)=\dfrac{2x}{x^2+1}=0\Rightarrow 2x=0$

$x=0$ is a stationary point, $f(0)=\ln(1)=0$

$f''(x)=\dfrac{2(x^2+1)-4x^2}{(x^2+1)^2}$ (with $u=2x$, $v=x^2+1$, $u'=2$, $v'=2x$)

$f''(0)=\dfrac{2(0+1)-0}{(0+1)^2}=2>0$ (concave up)

$\therefore(0,0)$ is a local minimum stationary point.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: f'(x) = 0 at x = 0; 1: stationary point (0, 0); 1: nature determined

$x^2=1$

Test:

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{373_q25_s1}

Area of base: $2x\times x=2x^2$, $\therefore$ cost of base: $15\times2x^2=\$30x^2$

$V=h\times2x\times x$, $90=2x^2h$, $h=\dfrac{45}{x^2}$

Area of sides: $2\times h\times2x+2\times x\times h=4xh+2xh=6xh=\dfrac{270}{x}$

Cost of sides $=20\times\dfrac{270}{x}=\$\dfrac{5400}{x}$

$\therefore$ total cost of tank, $C=30x^2+\dfrac{5400}{x}$

Trying to minimise cost: let $\dfrac{dC}{dx}=0$

$\dfrac{dC}{dx}=60x-\dfrac{5400}{x^2}=0$

$60x=\dfrac{5400}{x^2}$, $x^3=90$, $x=\sqrt[3]{90}$

Check that $\sqrt[3]{90}$ is a minimum point: $\dfrac{d^2C}{dx^2}=60+\dfrac{10800}{x^3}\Big|_{x=\sqrt[3]{90}}=2469\ldots>0$ (concave up)

$\therefore$ the minimum cost of the tank is when $x=\sqrt[3]{90}$

$\therefore$ dimensions of the tank are length $=2\sqrt[3]{90}$ m, width $=\sqrt[3]{90}$ m, height $=\dfrac{45}{\left(\sqrt[3]{90}\right)^2}=\dfrac{45}{90^{\frac23}}$ m.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: cost of base; 1: cost of sides; 1: total cost shown; 1: x = cube root of 90; 1: minimum verified and dimensions stated
review_reasons: guide evaluates the second derivative at x = cube root of 90 as 2469... (handwriting); correct value is 60 + 10800/90 = 180. Conclusion (minimum) unaffected; transcribed as written

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{373_q28_s1}

Find $P$: $2\tan x-1=\tan x$

$\tan x=1$

$x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ (1st solution)

Area $=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\tan x-(2\tan x-1)\,dx$

$=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}-\tan x+1\,dx$

$=\displaystyle\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\dfrac{-\sin x}{\cos x}+1\,dx=\Big[\ln(\cos x)+x\Big]_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}$

$=\left(\ln\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\right)+\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)-\left(\ln(1)-0\right)$

$=\ln\left(2^{-\frac12}\right)+\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$=-\dfrac12\ln2+\dfrac{\pi}{4}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: x-coordinate of P; 1: correct area integral; 1: correct primitive; 1: correct evaluation
1: correct primitive; 1: V(4) = 2V(5) used correctly; 1: C found; 1: correct expression for V
